decisions.statement: A value put into a list holding no value falls just inside the bracket.
A value put into a list already holding values falls after the last value.
A value written after another value is written behind a comma and a space.
A value put in order falls before the first value already written that sorts after it.
A value put in order that sorts after every value already written falls after the last of them.
A value is ordered against the others as each is written rather than as each reads.
A value is written as the caller spells that value.
A record put into a list falls after the records that list already holds.
A record takes the indent the record above it has.
A list written on one line gains its record on that line rather than on a line of its own.
A record put into a list holding none falls just inside the bracket.
An entry put into an object holding no entry falls just inside the brace on its own line.
An entry put into an object falls after the entry `after` names.
An entry falls after the last entry where `after` names no entry.
An entry written after another takes the indent that entry has.
The one entry a literal has goes with everything between that literal's delimiters.
An entry followed by a comma goes with that comma and with the space before the entry.
An entry followed by no comma goes back to where the entry before that entry ended.
An index naming no entry answers a span with nothing.
Nothing here reads the disk or the index.
Nothing here rewrites a body.
Nothing here judges whether an edit is wanted.

definition: the span an edit takes in an object literal or an array literal
